program.source: export function evaluate({ inputs, time }) { const launchSpeed = inputs.launchSpeed; const gravity = 9.8; const t = time; const height = launchSpeed * t - 0.5 * gravity * t * t; const velocity = launchSpeed - gravity * t; const apexTime = launchSpeed / gravity; const apexHeight = (launchSpeed * launchSpeed) / (2 * gravity); const laneY = 120; const ballY = laneY + 160 - Math.min(150, Math.max(0, height * 40)); const ballX = 320; let motionStateText = "Moving up"; if (Math.abs(velocity) < 0.05) { motionStateText = "Still for an instant"; } else if (velocity < 0) { motionStateText = "Moving down"; } const gravityStateText = "Gravity pulls down"; const lane = sdk.panel({ x: 60, y: 50, w: 520, h: 320, title: "Vertical Throw", state: motionStateText + ", " + gravityStateText, id: "lane.toss" }); const axis = sdk.axis("axis.height", { x: 100, y: 340, length: 240, orientation: "y", min: 0, max: 2.5, label: "Height", unit: "m" }); const guide = sdk.groundMark("mark.launch", ballX, 340, 60, "Launch"); const ball = sdk.circle("ball.toss", ballX, ballY, 28, { role: "output" }); let objects = [...lane, axis, guide, ball]; if (Math.abs(velocity) >= 0.05) { const vDir = velocity > 0 ? "up" : "down"; const vArr = sdk.vector("vec.v", { x: ballX + 24, y: ballY }, { value: Math.abs(velocity), direction: vDir }, { scale: 12, label: "v" }); objects.push(...vArr); } const aArr = sdk.vector("vec.a", { x: ballX - 36, y: ballY }, { value: gravity, direction: "down" }, { scale: 6, label: "a" }); objects.push(...aArr); const callout = sdk.callout(ballX + 50, ballY - 20, [motionStateText, gravityStateText], { id: "callout.toss" }); objects.push(callout); return { frame: { width: 640, height: 420, objects: objects, readouts: [{ id: "motionState", value: motionStateText }, { id: "gravityState", value: gravityStateText }] }, quantities: { launchSpeed, gravity, apexTime, apexHeight, velocity, height } }; }

manifest.title: The ball stops rising. Gravity doesn’t stop.
manifest.summary: Gravity slows the ball on the way up and speeds it up on the way down. At the top, the ball is still for an instant while gravity continues to pull it downward.
manifest.description: A vertical height scale shows a tossed ball moving up, pausing briefly at the apex, and falling back down. A blue vector arrow indicates vertical velocity, while a dashed warm vector arrow points downward continuously to represent constant gravitational acceleration.
manifest.instructions: Change launch speed, then press Play. At the top, playback pauses so you can inspect the arrows. Press Play again to watch the ball fall, or drag the timeline to inspect any moment.
